properties.title: ECG-WM: A Physiology-Informed ECG World Model for Clinical Intervention Simulation

membership.reason: Implements an action-conditioned latent DDPM world model regularized by a cardiac ODE prior (EPK) over clinical intervention steps, supporting multi-step rollout and candidate-medication comparison.

evidence_fragments.content: In this work, we propose an ECG World Model for action-conditioned predictive simulation of cardiac electrophysiology. Our framework integrates physiological ordinary differential equation (ODE) priors into latent diffusion dynamics through energy regularization. This structural guidance encourages the generation of physiologically plausible post-intervention ECG trajectories while reducing generative inconsistencies.

Specifically, given a pre-dose ECG signal xk at clinical step k, patient metadata d, and a candidate pharmacological intervention a, dedicated encoders extract the baseline cardiac state sk, the clinical condition embedding cd, and the intervention embedding ca. Building upon these representations, the core of our world model leverages a hybrid dynamics architecture to simulate the action-conditioned post-dose ECG xk+1. To mitigate physiological inconsistencies, an External Physiological Knowledge (EPK) module first translates the intervention a into a physiology-guided prior eepk by solving the underlying cardiac ODE.

To strictly prevent data leakage, each dataset is partitioned at the subject level based on patient IDs (about 8:2 train-test split) (more details in Appendix A): (1) MIMIC-IV-ECG & Clinical – By integrating MIMIC-IV-ECG (Gow et al., 2023) with MIMIC-IV-Clinical (Johnson et al., 2023), we align 12-lead ECG recordings with longitudinal patient EHRs. This enables multi-modal conditioning on demographics, lab results, and existing comorbidities. The dataset comprises 17,493 unique patients and 108,980 patient–drug episodes, with 3,090 distinct medications; (2) Drug-Response ECG Datasets – To evaluate drug-induced cardiac morphological effects, we utilize the ECGRDVQ (Johannesen et al., 2014) and ECGDMMLD (Johannesen et al., 2016) databases. These provide 7,763 valid high-fidelity ECGs from 43 subjects across eight distinct drug regimens; and (3) In-house OOD Dataset – To assess cross-dataset generalization, we test our model, trained primarily on the controlled drug-response cohorts, against an in-house dataset of MIMIC-IV ICU patients administered Verapamil.

[paraphrase (visual p.8)] Table 1 Post-dose ECG prediction on MIMIC-IV-ECG: Ours achieves Latent ECG MSE 0.045, MAE 0.159 and Signal ECG MSE 0.053, MAE 0.110, outperforming GLM-4.5 (0.095/0.164/0.062/0.125), GPT-5 mini (0.719/0.166/0.066/0.128), GPT-3.5 (0.424/0.285/0.265/0.232), GPT-4o (0.550/0.414/0.578/0.386), Qwen2.5-VL-7B (2.148/0.368/0.195/0.201), and MedGemma (5.655/0.899/0.561/0.349).

[paraphrase (visual p.9)] Table 2 ECG interval normality accuracy: Ours achieves QTc Acc 90.55±0.76% (Rec 96.26±0.82%), PR Acc 76.04±0.97% (Rec 80.84±1.24%), TpTe Acc 94.70±1.13% (Rec 95.06±0.49%). Table 3 OOD Verapamil generalization: Ours achieves Latent 0.068, Signal 0.084 vs DADM (0.080/0.119) and DiffuSETS (0.096/0.150). Table 4 diagnostic-change fidelity on 200 MIMIC-IV test cases (recorded medication): Ours achieves ΔRisk Pearson r=0.620, Spearman ρ=0.598, Sign Agreement 76%, MAE 0.0973, RMSE 0.1253 vs DADM (0.266, 0.255, 58%, 0.1291, 0.1625).

[paraphrase (visual p.14)] Figure 3, Figure 4, and Table 5 on MIMIC-IV-ECG autoregressive multi-step rollout vs oracle: Ours achieves Oracle 0.0572, Rollout 0.0580 (Δ=+0.0008), vs GPT-3.5 (0.0942/0.1036/+0.0094), GPT-4o (0.1124/0.1245/+0.0121), and GPT-5-mini (0.1025/0.1172/+0.0147); removing EPK loss increases one-step Latent MSE from 0.045 to 0.061 and Signal MSE from 0.053 to 0.060.
They do not establish calibrated clinical risk, causal treatment effects, or the benefit of selecting an alternative medication.
the model lacks calibrated uncertainty estimates and formal safety guarantees, constraining its use in high-stakes settings. Accordingly, the system should not be used as a standalone clinical tool
On 1,273 hospitalization chains, ewm8 achieves 98.7% retention with an additional mean latent MSE of only 0.000882.

[paraphrase (visual p.17)] Appendix B.6 / Figure 6 illustrates a single-patient counterfactual drug-response simulation from one normal pre-dose ECG across three candidate drugs: Dofetilide (MSE 0.0333, QTc 419.3 ms, PR 201.7 ms, TpTe 78.4 ms), Ranolazine (MSE 0.0418, QTc 352.7 ms, PR 213.3 ms, TpTe 63.7 ms), and the administered Verapamil (MSE 0.0193, QTc 379.1 ms, PR 210.0 ms, TpTe 88.2 ms).

capability_assessments.rationale: Action-conditioned latent DDPM + cardiac ODE world model quantitatively evaluated on single-step post-dose ECG waveform, interval, OOD Verapamil, and diagnostic-change prediction (Tables 1-4, 9, 11-12) and short-chain multi-step rollouts (Tables 5, 13), supporting L2. Downgraded from L3 because all quantitative tables evaluate only the single recorded medication a_true, Top-1 candidate concordance values discussed in Appendix E.7 are not reported, and Appendix B.6 / Figure 6 shows only an N=1 illustrative 3-drug comparison.

limitations: Discrete medication tokens without continuous pharmacokinetic dosing.
Uncalibrated diagnostic-proxy scores; no causal identification or prospective clinical evaluation.

All quantitative tables (Tables 1-14) evaluate only the single recorded medication; Top-1 candidate-ranking concordance described in Appendix E.7 is not quantitatively reported, and matched alternative-drug simulation is shown only for a single exemplar case (Appendix B.6, Figure 6).
notes: All 35 physical PDF pages read (1-20 inherited + 21-35 read directly); Figures 2, 3, 4, 5 and Tables 1-15 inspected.

legacy_cells.B: ECG-WM: A Physiology-Informed ECG World Model for Clinical Intervention Simulation
legacy_cells.C: Zhikang Chen; Yue Wang; Sen Cui; Yu Zhang; Changshui Zhang; Tianling Ren; Tingting Zhu
legacy_cells.S: For a pre-dose ECG and candidate medication, what post-dose ECG trajectory and diagnostic-proxy change does the model predict?
legacy_cells.T: The MIMIC-IV clinical cohort comprises 17,493 patients; controlled drug-response ECG datasets comprise 43 subjects across eight regimens, with an additional MIMIC-IV ICU verapamil OOD cohort.
legacy_cells.AI: 12-lead ECG waveforms; clinical metadata (demographics, laboratory results, comorbidities); discrete pharmacological intervention tokens
legacy_cells.AJ: Pre-trained VAE encoder for ECG; dedicated encoders for clinical-condition and intervention embeddings (specific architectures not stated)
legacy_cells.AK: Pre-trained VAE on MIMIC-IV-ECG, kept frozen
legacy_cells.BD: Discrete medication or regimen labels; combination regimens are categorical actions; experimental action representation uses discrete tokens rather than continuous dosage
legacy_cells.BN: McSharry cardiac-phase ECG ODE; pharmacology-informed rule-based parameter modulation; latent squared-distance energy regularization toward the projected ODE trajectory
legacy_cells.BS: Generated post-dose ECG waveforms decoded from the next latent state; downstream frozen ECG foundation model produces diagnostic-proxy scores
legacy_cells.BT: Frozen ECG foundation model with 17 diagnostic-label probabilities, aggregated into a scalar diagnostic-risk proxy
legacy_cells.BU: Candidate score S(a) = mean diagnostic-proxy score µR(a) + λ times its standard deviation σR(a)
legacy_cells.BV: DDPM noise-prediction squared error plus λEPK-weighted squared distance between predicted clean latent and projected physiological anchor
legacy_cells.CA: NVIDIA A800-SXM4-80G GPUs (80 GB HBM2e); local Linux server with AMD EPYC 7742 64-core CPU
legacy_cells.CD: Maximum evaluated recorded-chain length: 6 steps (reported as rows; elapsed time not stated)
legacy_cells.CG: Five stochastic DDPM samples per candidate intervention for diagnostic-proxy evaluation
legacy_cells.FN: On 200 subject-disjoint MIMIC-IV cases, predicted diagnostic-score changes had Pearson r=0.620, Spearman rho=0.598 and 76% sign agreement; MAE 0.0973 and RMSE 0.1253. Table 4 reports one sampling run; repeated samples assess stochastic-generation variation, not training-seed or population uncertainty.
legacy_cells.FR: Comparative drug-response simulations and observational post-dose diagnostic-change agreement do not identify causal effects or calibrated clinical risk. Frozen diagnostic-score agreement, qualitative alternative-drug examples and stochastic-sampling variation do not establish prospective treatment benefit.
